name: two-stage-dcf
description: Two-stage enterprise valuation from a company's financial statements and text, fetched for a ticker (statements and 10-Ks from SEC EDGAR, press releases from 8-Ks, call transcripts from the Motley Fool) or read from a folder. Classifies every reported balance-sheet line and foots it, computes the historical driver ratios with a script, reads the MD&A, transcripts and press releases for evidence on each driver, and writes one HTML page with four tabs: Line items (the classification), Forecasts (the argument for each assumption with quoted citations), an editable Baseline grid, and DCF, which revalues in the browser as the Baseline is edited, with a measured ranking of what moves the answer. The numbers live in a CSV that rebuilds the page, so the assumptions can be argued over and revised; when they are settled it delivers an Excel workbook whose model is live formulas, with sensitivity and driver-ranking sheets and a Check sheet that goes red if the formulas ever disagree with the Python engine.
